title: Restore substantial scalp hair in severe alopecia areata with systemic treatment

concept.text: Reverse extensive autoimmune hair loss through an approved systemic medicine. JAK-pathway treatment achieved clinically substantial regrowth in a subset of patients, without establishing permanent immune tolerance. Proposed completion test: FDA approval supported by randomized trials in patients with at least 50% scalp hair loss, demonstrating superiority to placebo in achieving SALT ≤20, equivalent to at least 80% scalp hair coverage. Test set by: FDA; the baricitinib trials evaluated the SALT ≤20 endpoint at week 36. Reported achieved: FDA approved baricitinib (Olumiant) for adults with severe alopecia areata on 13 June 2022. Overlaps: DER-03, IMM-04. Sources given: [FDA announcement of first systemic alopecia areata treatment](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USFDA/bulletins/31bfc85) ; [FDA review describing the alopecia treatment landscape](https://www.fda.gov/media/172964/download?attachment=).
source_urls: [FDA announcement of first systemic alopecia areata treatment](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USFDA/bulletins/31bfc85)

page.title: Systemic treatment of severe alopecia areata
page.definition: An approved medicine acting throughout the body restores at least 80% scalp hair coverage in some adults with alopecia areata, an autoimmune attack on hair follicles, who initially had at least 50% scalp hair loss. Response is measured with the Severity of Alopecia Tool (SALT), which scores percentage scalp hair loss.

goal.need: In 2022, FDA reported that alopecia areata affected more than 300,000 people in the United States each year. In two pivotal trials enrolling adults with at least 50% scalp hair loss for more than six months, only 3–5% of placebo recipients reached at least 80% scalp hair coverage after 36 weeks.

completion.title: FDA approves a systemic medicine for adults with severe alopecia areata.
completion.criterion: FDA grants marketing approval for a systemic medicine to treat adults with severe alopecia areata. This test was met by oral baricitinib on 13 June 2022. Its supporting trials enrolled 1,200 adults with at least 50% scalp hair loss for more than six months and assessed SALT ≤20, equivalent to at least 80% scalp hair coverage, at week 36. These numerical conditions describe the supporting trials rather than a universal FDA approval rule.
completion.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, NDA 207924/S-007 approval letter and accompanying prescribing information.
completion.threshold_quote: It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling.
completion.basis: The capability is an approved systemic treatment producing scalp hair regrowth in severe alopecia areata. FDA explicitly identified baricitinib as the first systemic treatment approved for this disease. The approval letter establishes authorization, and the prescribing information identifies the population and hair-coverage endpoint supporting it.

milestones.title: JAK inhibition restores complete hair coverage in treated mouse skin within 12 weeks.
milestones.criterion: A Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor reverses established alopecia areata in treated skin of C3H/HeJ mice, with complete hair regrowth within 12 weeks. Xing and colleagues reported this in 2014 using topical ruxolitinib or tofacitinib: three mice per group in each of three experiments, giving nine mice per treatment group and nine vehicle controls. This establishes an animal proof of mechanism; systemic treatment is tested in the subsequent human milestones.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback: searches of FDA approval documents and alopecia areata guidelines found no standardized animal efficacy threshold. The criterion follows the complete-regrowth result in Xing and colleagues' published experiment.

milestones.title: Oral JAK inhibition reduces scalp hair loss by at least 50% in people with alopecia areata.
milestones.criterion: Participants meet the registered ruxolitinib pilot's responder definition: at least 50% improvement from baseline in scalp hair loss measured by SALT at the end of treatment. Initial human evidence appeared in 2014 in three patients with regrowth over 3–5 months. The completed open-label study, published in 2016, treated 12 patients with moderate-to-severe alopecia areata using oral ruxolitinib 20 mg twice daily for 3–6 months; nine of 12 met the endpoint. The uncontrolled design does not establish superiority to placebo.
milestones.set_by: Columbia University investigators, registered protocol NCT01950780, with the prespecified endpoint reported by Mackay-Wiggan and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary endpoint was the proportion of subjects with 50% or greater hair regrowth from baseline to end of treatment.

milestones.title: A phase 2 systemic treatment beats placebo for at least 80% scalp coverage at week 36.
milestones.criterion: A randomized phase 2 trial in adults with baseline SALT ≥50 demonstrates superiority to placebo on the proportion reaching SALT ≤20 at week 36. In BRAVE-AA1, published in 2021, 110 adults were randomized: placebo, 28; baricitinib 1 mg daily, 28; 2 mg daily, 27; and 4 mg daily, 27. Response was 33.3% with 2 mg and 51.9% with 4 mg versus 3.6% with placebo, with P=.016 and P=.001, respectively. Missing outcomes were treated as nonresponses.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly and Company and BRAVE-AA1 investigators, phase 2 protocol NCT03570749, reported by King and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving a Severity of Alopecia Tool (SALT) score ≤20 at week 36.

milestones.title: Systemic treatment beats placebo for ≥80% scalp coverage at week 36 in two phase 3 trials.
milestones.criterion: Two randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials in adults with baseline SALT ≥50 demonstrate superiority on the proportion reaching SALT ≤20 at week 36. BRAVE-AA1 enrolled 654 adults and BRAVE-AA2 enrolled 546. FDA's analysis reported responses with baricitinib 4 mg daily of 35% versus 5% with placebo in AA-1, and 32% versus 3% in AA-2; both estimated differences were 30 percentage points, with 95% confidence intervals of 23–36 percentage points. The peer-reviewed trials were published on 26 March 2022.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly and Company and BRAVE-AA investigators, phase 3 protocols NCT03570749 and NCT03899259; FDA reports the regulatory response estimates in prescribing-information section 14.3.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary outcome was a SALT score of 20 or less at week 36.

not_found: No regulator or professional-society threshold for preclinical hair-regrowth efficacy was found.
The supplied FDA review at media/172964 could not be opened because its PDF exceeded the retrieval size limit.
No public FDA authorization letter for the initial alopecia areata clinical trials was found.

results.finding: C3H/HeJ mice with established alopecia areata: 9 per treatment group; complete hair regrowth within 12 weeks.
results.detail: Topical ruxolitinib and tofacitinib were applied to affected back skin. Each treatment and vehicle group included three mice per experiment across three experiments.
results.quote: A full coat of hair emerged in the ruxolitinib- or tofacitinib-treated mice by 7 weeks of treatment (data not shown), and we observed complete hair regrowth within 12 weeks following topical therapy (

results.finding: In 12 patients with moderate-to-severe alopecia areata, 9 achieved at least 50% hair regrowth with oral ruxolitinib.
results.detail: The primary endpoint measured regrowth from baseline by SALT at the end of 3–6 months of treatment. The open-label study did not establish superiority to placebo.
results.quote: Nine of twelve patients (75%) had significant hair regrowth and achieved the primary outcome of at least 50% regrowth

results.finding: In 110 adults, 51.9% receiving baricitinib 4 mg reached SALT ≤20 at week 36.
results.detail: The 2-mg group also exceeded placebo: 33.3% versus 3.6%. Missing outcomes were imputed as nonresponses.
results.quote: At week 36, the proportion of patients achieving a SALT score of ≤20 was significantly greater in baricitinib 2-mg (33.3%, P = .016) and 4-mg (51.9%, P = .001) groups versus placebo (3.6%).

results.finding: BRAVE-AA1 and AA2 (654 and 546 adults): baricitinib 4 mg exceeded placebo by 32.6 percentage points for SALT ≤20 at week 36 in each trial.
results.detail: Both trials were randomized and placebo-controlled, with baseline SALT ≥50. The paper's estimates differ from the FDA analysis cited in the criterion.
results.quote: The estimated percentage of patients with a SALT score of 20 or less at week 36 was 38.8% with 4-mg baricitinib, 22.8% with 2-mg baricitinib, and 6.2% with placebo in BRAVE-AA1 and 35.9%, 19.4%, and 3.3%, respectively, in BRAVE-AA2.

results.finding: FDA approved baricitinib tablets for adults with severe alopecia areata on 13 June 2022; sample size not reported.
results.detail: The approval letter does not report the supporting trial sample size or SALT outcomes.
